comment: Scholar loop work queue. One unit per scholar tick. Each unit becomes a mechanism/era card in corpus/cards/. The scholar may append units it discovers (snowball), tagged discovered_by: scholar. Order = priority.

units.topic: Ancient race games: Senet, Royal Game of Ur, Hounds & Jackals — what 4,500 years of survival says about luck-vs-skill dosing
Go and the economy of one rule — depth from placement + capture alone; what minimal rulesets buy
Chess lineage (chaturanga→shogi→chess): asymmetric piece powers, drop rules, why shogi never goes stale
Mancala family: perfect-information sowing engines, ruleset variation across Africa/Asia as natural A/B testing
Backgammon: the doubling cube as the greatest tension invention; racing + luck management
Dexterity games that sold: Jenga, Crokinole, Carrom, ICECOOL, Klask — physical skill as the fun engine and its party-context dependence
Physical hidden-state machines: Stay Alive (1965), Screwball Scramble, Mouse Trap — what breaks and what delights in plastic mechanisms
The German school: Catan, Carcassonne, El Grande — interaction without elimination, catch-up mechanics, 60-minute discipline
Engine builders: Dominion, Splendor, Wingspan — the compounding-growth dopamine curve and its endgame problem
Auction/valuation: Knizia's trilogy (Ra, Modern Art, Tigris) — pricing as gameplay; why auctions died in mass market
Worker placement: Agricola, Viticulture — blocking as interaction; turn-order tension
Social deduction: Werewolf, The Resistance, Blood on the Clocktower — hidden roles, table talk, player-count sensitivity
Cooperative engines: Pandemic, Spirit Island, The Crew — alpha-player problem and solutions; co-op difficulty tuning
Legacy/campaign: Risk Legacy, Pandemic Legacy, Gloomhaven — permanent change as retention; the reset economics
Roll-and-write boom: Qwixx, Welcome To, Cartographers — why paper+pencil beat apps; simultaneous play
Abstract modern: Hive, Azul, Santorini, YINSH (GIPF) — theme-free depth, piece-geometry-as-rules (Hive has no board!)
Party geometry: Codenames, Wavelength, Just One — the spectator problem solved; one clever constraint per game
Yavalath and LUDI: the computer-invented game that sold — Browne's fitness function (drama, uncertainty, depth proxies), what it validates for Bob
Failed physical games post-2015 (Kickstarter graveyard): overproduced minis, rules bloat, kinetic gimmicks that bored after one play — the anti-canon
3D-printed games on marketplaces today (Printables/MakerWorld/Etsy): what exists, what sells, where the white space is
Trick-taking 500 years on: from Karnöffel to The Crew — why the oldest card mechanism keeps producing hits
Tension mechanics inventory: push-your-luck (Can't Stop, Quacks), timers, bag-building — quantifying 'one more turn'
Player-count reality: BGG data on 2p vs 3-4p vs party sizes; what player count Bob should design for first and why
Rulebook science: how the best rulebooks teach (Uwe/Leacock patterns), ambiguity failure modes, the 'first game in 5 minutes' bar
